https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-.snippet: # How to Implement Default Deny Network Policies in Kubernetes. Learn how to implement default deny network policies in Kubernetes to create a zero-trust network model for your cluster. ## Deny All Ingress Traffic. # deny-all-ingress.yaml # Block all incoming traffic to every pod in this namespace apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: deny-all-ingress namespace: production spec: # Empty selector matches ALL pods in the namespace podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Ingress # No ingress rules means no traffic is allowed in. # deny-all-egress.yaml # Block all outgoing traffic from every pod in this namespace apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: deny-all-egress namespace: production spec: # Empty selector matches ALL pods podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Egress # No egress rules means no outbound traffic is allowed. ## Deny All Ingress and Egress. # deny-all-traffic.yaml # Block all traffic in both directions for every pod apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: deny-all-traffic namespace: production spec: podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Ingress - Egress # No rules at all - everything is blocked.
